chunks.title: Why Vireek was started
chunks.content: Vireek was built by a single founder (Ali) who spent time around home-service businesses and saw how often the phone goes unanswered -- mid-job, after hours, during a rush. Existing options were unsatisfying: a full-time receptionist is expensive and still has off-hours; generic answering services can take a message but cannot qualify a lead, tell a tripped breaker from a tripped GFCI, or book a job; voicemail just sits there. Vireek was built as something purpose-made for the trades instead of a generic answering script.

chunks.title: Vireek's stated values
chunks.content: Radical Transparency -- no fake testimonials, invented customer counts, or hidden pricing; what you see is what you get. Built for One Industry, Done Right -- Vireek focuses on home-service businesses rather than being a generic receptionist for everyone. Always Improving -- the product is continuously iterated based on direct customer feedback. Follow Through -- the product should not just answer calls, it should move the conversation to the next real step (a booked job, a flagged emergency), not just take a message.

chunks.title: What Vireek is
chunks.content: Vireek is an AI voice receptionist built specifically for home-service businesses (HVAC, plumbing, roofing, electrical, restoration, locksmith). Its receptionist persona is named "Sarah." Sarah answers every call 24/7, captures lead details, books appointments, and flags emergencies so a missed call never becomes a lost job.

chunks.title: Team, culture, and hiring
chunks.content: Vireek is a small, early, remote-first team with flexible hours. There is a direct line to the founder -- decisions happen in conversation, not through layers of management. The company describes itself honestly as small ("not a 500-person company pretending to be scrappy"). Early team members get meaningful equity. If there's no open role listed that fits, people can email ali@vireek.com to introduce themselves for future roles.

chunks.title: Emergency calls -- what Vireek does and does not do
chunks.content: Vireek can identify urgent/emergency language, collect key details, and flag time-sensitive calls for immediate follow-up or dispatch, based on rules the business configures. IMPORTANT: Vireek is NOT a replacement for emergency services (911/fire/police/ambulance). It helps a home-service business avoid missing an urgent customer call -- it does not handle life-safety emergency dispatch itself. Never tell a caller or user that Vireek replaces calling emergency services.

chunks.title: Is Vireek a real person answering the phone?
chunks.content: No. Vireek is AI software designed to sound natural, understand caller intent, and collect the information the business needs. Vireek never impersonates a human when a caller directly asks whether they're talking to an AI.

chunks.title: Do I need a new phone number? How long does setup take?
chunks.content: No new phone number is required in most cases -- a business typically keeps its existing number and forwards calls to Vireek, so customers keep using the number they already know. Setup is designed to be fast: provide business information, configure call-handling preferences, and connect the phone-forwarding flow; no hardware install is required.

chunks.content: Vireek can handle most front-desk call-answering and intake tasks, especially after hours or during peak call volume, and on Professional plans and above it can warm-transfer a call live to on-call staff. Many businesses use it to support their existing staff rather than fully replace human judgment for complex situations -- position it as "never miss a call" coverage, not a guaranteed total replacement for every human interaction.

chunks.content: Call transcripts and summaries are stored so the business's team can review conversations and follow up; access is limited to the account and any team members granted permission. Billing is handled by a dedicated payment processor -- Vireek does not store raw card details on its own servers. Infrastructure runs in the United States today. Full data-location detail and the sub-processor list live at vireek.com/trust; legal terms are at vireek.com/privacy and vireek.com/terms.

chunks.title: Compliance certifications -- what Vireek does NOT currently hold
chunks.content: IMPORTANT GUARDRAIL: Vireek's public Security page is deliberately written as factual statements about how the platform is built (encryption in transit/at rest, RLS-based account isolation, role-based access) rather than claiming a compliance certification the company does not hold. As of the last content update, Vireek does not claim SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, or ISO 27001 certification. The AI must NEVER tell a customer or prospect that Vireek is "SOC 2 compliant," "HIPAA compliant," or holds any other specific certification unless this file is updated to say so explicitly. If asked about a specific certification, say that Vireek does not currently publish that certification and suggest contacting ali@vireek.com or booking a demo to discuss specific compliance requirements before signing up.

chunks.title: How Vireek protects data (technical pillars)
chunks.content: All traffic between the browser, the Vireek dashboard, and its database runs over TLS, and data at rest is encrypted by the infrastructure provider. Every account's calls, leads, and jobs are protected by Postgres row-level security (RLS) policies, so one business can never query or see another business's data. Account owners control role-based team permissions (billing, team management, business-profile editing, viewing all jobs) down to the individual permission. Escalation rules, greetings, and business details are fully configured by the account owner -- nothing is shared with a caller that wasn't configured by the business.

chunks.title: Reporting a security vulnerability
chunks.content: Vireek welcomes responsible disclosure of security vulnerabilities. Reports can be sent to ali@vireek.com, or via the machine-readable security.txt file (RFC 9116) at vireek.com/.well-known/security.txt. The full Vulnerability Disclosure Policy is at vireek.com/vulnerability-disclosure.

chunks.title: After-Hours Answering
chunks.content: After-Hours Answering: Handling calls that come in outside normal business hours — nights, weekends, holidays — when most home service businesses would otherwise send callers to voicemail.

chunks.title: AI Agent
chunks.content: AI Agent: A software system that can carry out a task on its own — such as answering a call, asking qualifying questions, and logging the result — rather than simply responding to a single prompt. An AI voice receptionist is a specific type of AI agent focused on phone conversations.

chunks.title: Hallucination (AI)
chunks.content: Hallucination (AI): When an AI system states something false or invented with apparent confidence — for example, quoting a price or policy that was never configured. Well-built voice AI systems constrain responses to verified business information to minimize this risk.

chunks.title: AI Voice Receptionist
chunks.content: AI Voice Receptionist: Software that answers incoming phone calls in a natural-sounding voice, asks qualifying questions, and captures caller details the way a human front-desk employee would — without breaks, sick days, or after-hours gaps. Vireek’s AI voice receptionist, Sarah, is built specifically for home service businesses.

chunks.title: Answer Rate
chunks.content: Answer Rate: The percentage of inbound calls that are actually answered, as opposed to going to voicemail or ringing out. A low answer rate is one of the clearest warning signs of lost revenue for a home service business.

chunks.title: API Integration
chunks.content: API Integration: A connection between two software systems that lets them exchange data automatically, such as sending a captured lead from an AI receptionist directly into a CRM without manual entry.

chunks.title: Appointment Booking
chunks.content: Appointment Booking: Scheduling a service visit directly during the initial call or follow-up, ideally synced to a live calendar so double-bookings and scheduling conflicts are avoided.

chunks.title: Audit Log
chunks.content: Audit Log: A recorded history of sensitive actions taken within a system, such as permission changes or deleted records, so administrators can review exactly what happened and when.

chunks.title: Average Handle Time (AHT)
chunks.content: Average Handle Time (AHT): The average length of a call from answer to hang-up, including any hold or transfer time. AHT is a useful efficiency metric, but should be balanced against call quality — a shorter call isn’t better if it skips important details.

chunks.title: Barge-In
chunks.content: Barge-In: The ability for a caller to interrupt the AI mid-sentence and have it stop talking and listen, the same way a human would naturally yield the floor. Systems without barge-in feel stiff because callers have to wait out a full prompt before speaking.

chunks.title: Booking Rate
chunks.content: Booking Rate: The share of answered calls that result in a scheduled appointment. A well-run call process — whether human or AI — aims to move a ready caller to booking quickly rather than over-qualifying them.

chunks.title: Call Abandonment Rate
chunks.content: Call Abandonment Rate: The percentage of callers who hang up before their call is answered, often because of long hold times or a confusing phone menu. This metric is closely tied to lost job opportunities in home service businesses.

chunks.title: Call Analytics
chunks.content: Call Analytics: Reporting on call volume, answer rates, call outcomes, and trends over time, used to spot patterns like which hours generate the most missed calls or which service type drives the most inquiries.

chunks.title: Call Forwarding
chunks.content: Call Forwarding: Redirecting calls from one number to another automatically — for example, forwarding your existing business line to Vireek so customers keep dialing the number they already know while an AI receptionist answers.

chunks.title: Call Overflow
chunks.content: Call Overflow: What happens to calls that arrive when your team is already on the phone or unavailable. Overflow calls are the ones most likely to go to voicemail unless a backup system, such as an AI receptionist, is in place to catch them.

chunks.title: Call Queue
chunks.content: Call Queue: A holding line for calls waiting to be answered when every available line or agent is busy. Long queues increase the chance a caller hangs up before ever speaking to anyone.

chunks.title: Call Recording
chunks.content: Call Recording: An audio capture of a phone conversation, kept for quality review, training, or dispute resolution. Recordings are typically stored alongside a transcript and should be protected with the same access controls as other customer data.

chunks.title: Call Routing
chunks.content: Call Routing: The logic that decides where an inbound call should go — a specific technician, a department, voicemail, or an AI receptionist — often based on time of day, caller history, or the reason for the call.

chunks.title: Call Script
chunks.content: Call Script: The structured set of questions and talking points used to handle a call consistently — not necessarily word-for-word dialogue, but a defined order of information to gather, such as service needed, location, and urgency.

chunks.title: Call Summarization
chunks.content: Call Summarization: An AI-generated summary of a phone call that highlights the key details — the issue reported, the address, the urgency level — so a technician or office manager can get up to speed in seconds instead of reading a full transcript.

chunks.title: Call Transcription
chunks.content: Call Transcription: A written, searchable record of everything said during a call. Transcripts let office staff review what an AI receptionist captured without having to re-listen to the full audio recording.

chunks.title: Caller ID
chunks.content: Caller ID: The information displayed about an incoming call, typically the caller’s phone number and sometimes their name, used to identify returning customers before the call is even answered.

chunks.title: Cold Transfer
chunks.content: Cold Transfer: A call transfer where the caller is passed along with no context given to the receiving person, forcing the customer to re-explain their issue from the beginning.

chunks.title: Conversational AI
chunks.content: Conversational AI: A class of AI systems designed to hold natural, back-and-forth conversations rather than follow a rigid script or menu tree. Conversational AI understands follow-up questions, interruptions, and context from earlier in the same call.

chunks.title: Conversion Rate
chunks.content: Conversion Rate: The percentage of leads or calls that turn into actual booked jobs. Improving answer rates and call quality both tend to move this number directly.

chunks.title: Cost Per Lead (CPL)
chunks.content: Cost Per Lead (CPL): How much a business spends, on average, to generate a single lead through advertising or marketing. CPL only tells half the story if a meaningful share of those leads are then lost to missed calls.

chunks.title: CRM (Customer Relationship Management)
chunks.content: CRM (Customer Relationship Management): Software used to track customers, leads, and job history in one place. Syncing call data into a CRM automatically avoids double data entry and keeps every team member working from the same information.

chunks.title: Customer Lifetime Value (CLV)
chunks.content: Customer Lifetime Value (CLV): The total revenue a business can expect from a single customer across the full relationship, including repeat service calls, maintenance plans, and referrals — not just the first job.

chunks.title: Data Encryption
chunks.content: Data Encryption: Converting data into a coded form that can only be read with the correct decryption key, protecting sensitive information such as customer addresses and call transcripts from unauthorized access.

chunks.title: Data Retention Policy
chunks.content: Data Retention Policy: The rules a company sets for how long it keeps different types of data, such as call recordings or transcripts, before securely deleting them.

chunks.title: Dispatch
chunks.content: Dispatch: The process of assigning a job to a technician and sending them to the customer’s location, usually based on location, availability, and skill set.

chunks.title: DTMF (Dual-Tone Multi-Frequency)
chunks.content: DTMF (Dual-Tone Multi-Frequency): The technical name for the tones generated when someone presses a button on a phone keypad — the sound behind old-school "press 1 for sales" menus.

chunks.title: Electrical Contractor
chunks.content: Electrical Contractor: A licensed professional or business that installs, repairs, and maintains electrical wiring and systems in homes and buildings.

chunks.title: Encryption at Rest
chunks.content: Encryption at Rest: Encrypting data while it is stored on a disk or in a database, so that even if the underlying storage were somehow accessed directly, the data itself would remain unreadable.

chunks.title: Encryption in Transit
chunks.content: Encryption in Transit: Encrypting data while it travels between systems — for example, between a caller’s phone and Vireek’s servers — so it cannot be intercepted and read along the way.

chunks.title: Field Service Management (FSM)
chunks.content: Field Service Management (FSM): Software platforms built specifically for scheduling, dispatching, and managing technicians who work at customer locations, such as ServiceTitan, Housecall Pro, or Jobber.

chunks.title: First Call Resolution (FCR)
chunks.content: First Call Resolution (FCR): The percentage of caller issues fully resolved during the initial call, without needing a callback or additional follow-up. Higher FCR generally means happier customers and less repeat work for the office.

chunks.title: Flat-Rate Pricing
chunks.content: Flat-Rate Pricing: A pricing model where the customer is quoted a fixed price for a specific job before work begins, regardless of how long the job actually takes.

chunks.title: Follow-Up Automation
chunks.content: Follow-Up Automation: Automatically reaching back out to leads or customers — through text, email, or a scheduled callback — without relying on someone remembering to do it manually.

chunks.title: GDPR
chunks.content: GDPR: The General Data Protection Regulation — a European Union law governing how personal data is collected, stored, and used, with significant requirements around consent and the right to have data deleted.

chunks.title: Hold Time
chunks.content: Hold Time: The amount of time a caller spends waiting before reaching a live person or getting a response. Extended hold times are one of the leading causes of caller abandonment.

chunks.title: Home Service Business
chunks.content: Home Service Business: A company that performs work at a customer’s home or property, such as HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roofing, restoration, or locksmith services — the core market Vireek is built for.

chunks.title: HVAC
chunks.content: HVAC: Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning — the trade responsible for installing, repairing, and maintaining home climate-control systems. HVAC businesses see some of the sharpest seasonal call spikes of any home service trade.

chunks.title: Intent Recognition
chunks.content: Intent Recognition: The process of identifying what a caller actually wants — booking a repair, checking on an existing job, asking about pricing — from the words they use, even when they phrase the request differently than expected.

chunks.title: IVR (Interactive Voice Response)
chunks.content: IVR (Interactive Voice Response): The older "press 1 for sales, press 2 for support" phone menu technology. IVR routes calls based on button presses rather than understanding natural speech, which is why it frustrates callers with anything but the simplest requests.

chunks.title: Job Costing
chunks.content: Job Costing: Tracking the actual labor, materials, and overhead cost of completing a specific job, used to measure profitability per job rather than just per customer or per month.

chunks.title: Latency (Voice AI)
chunks.content: Latency (Voice AI): The delay between when a caller finishes speaking and when the AI responds. Low latency is critical for a natural-feeling conversation — noticeable pauses make callers think the line dropped or the system is confused.

chunks.title: Lead Capture
chunks.content: Lead Capture: The process of collecting a prospective customer’s contact information and service request as soon as they reach out, so no interested caller falls through the cracks before your team follows up.

chunks.title: Lead Qualification
chunks.content: Lead Qualification: Asking a defined set of questions to determine whether a caller is a good fit — inside the service area, a real job rather than a spam call, and clear about what they need — before dispatching a technician.

chunks.title: Lead Scoring
chunks.content: Lead Scoring: Ranking incoming leads by how likely they are to convert into paying jobs, based on factors like urgency, service type, and location, so the highest-value opportunities get followed up first.

chunks.title: Live Transfer
chunks.content: Live Transfer: Connecting a caller directly to a live person in real time, often after an AI or automated system has already gathered the initial details — used for urgent or high-value calls that need immediate human judgment.

chunks.title: Large Language Model (LLM)
chunks.content: Large Language Model (LLM): An AI model trained on large amounts of text that can understand and generate human-like language. LLMs power the reasoning behind modern conversational AI, including how an AI receptionist decides which question to ask next.

chunks.title: Local Number
chunks.content: Local Number: A phone number with an area code matching the business’s service region. Local numbers tend to build more trust with nearby customers than an unfamiliar toll-free or out-of-area number.

chunks.title: Locksmith
chunks.content: Locksmith: A tradesperson specializing in locks, keys, and security hardware, frequently called for lockouts that require an immediate response regardless of time of day.

chunks.title: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
chunks.content: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): A login security method requiring more than just a password — typically a code from a phone or authenticator app — to confirm a user’s identity and reduce the risk of unauthorized account access.

chunks.title: Missed Call Cost
chunks.content: Missed Call Cost: An estimate of the revenue lost from unanswered calls, typically calculated from call volume, close rate, and average ticket size. Many home service businesses are surprised how large this number is once they run it.

chunks.title: Missed Call
chunks.content: Missed Call: An inbound call that goes unanswered, whether it rings out, hits voicemail, or is declined. For home service businesses, a missed call is rarely a callback opportunity — most callers move straight to the next business on their list.

chunks.title: Natural Language Processing (NLP)
chunks.content: Natural Language Processing (NLP): The branch of AI that lets software understand and generate human language. NLP is what allows an AI receptionist to parse a caller saying "my AC stopped blowing cold air" and recognize it as a no-cool HVAC issue rather than a billing question.

chunks.title: No-Heat / No-Cool Call
chunks.content: No-Heat / No-Cool Call: Industry shorthand for an HVAC emergency call where a customer’s heating or cooling system has stopped working entirely — these calls spike during extreme weather and rarely wait for business hours.

chunks.title: No-Show Rate
chunks.content: No-Show Rate: The percentage of booked appointments where the customer isn’t present or available when the technician arrives, often reduced with confirmation calls or reminder messages.

chunks.title: PCI DSS
chunks.content: PCI DSS: The Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard — a set of requirements for any business that handles credit card information, designed to reduce the risk of payment data breaches.

chunks.title: Plumbing
chunks.content: Plumbing: The trade covering water supply, drainage, and gas piping systems in homes and buildings. Plumbing emergencies like burst pipes are highly time-sensitive and often arrive outside business hours.

chunks.title: Preventive Maintenance (PM)
chunks.content: Preventive Maintenance (PM): Scheduled service performed to keep equipment running well and catch small problems before they become expensive repairs — common for HVAC systems, water heaters, and other home equipment.

chunks.title: QuickBooks Sync
chunks.content: QuickBooks Sync: Automatically connecting call and job data with QuickBooks accounting records, reducing manual bookkeeping and keeping invoicing aligned with actual completed work.

chunks.title: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
chunks.content: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): A security model that grants different levels of access based on a person’s role — for example, a technician sees only their assigned jobs, while an office manager sees the full call and lead history.

chunks.title: Restoration Company
chunks.content: Restoration Company: A business that responds to water, fire, mold, or storm damage to restore a property to its prior condition — work that is almost always urgent and unplanned by the customer.

chunks.title: Revenue Leakage
chunks.content: Revenue Leakage: Revenue a business should have earned but lost due to operational gaps — missed calls, slow follow-up, or dropped leads — rather than a lack of demand.

chunks.title: Roofing Contractor
chunks.content: Roofing Contractor: A business specializing in roof installation, repair, and replacement — often fielding a high volume of storm-related emergency calls in short bursts.

chunks.title: Route Optimization
chunks.content: Route Optimization: Planning technician schedules and driving routes to minimize travel time between jobs, allowing more appointments to be completed in a day.

chunks.title: Row Level Security (RLS)
chunks.content: Row Level Security (RLS): A database-level protection that restricts which rows of data a given account can read or write, enforced by the database itself rather than only by application code. Vireek scopes every policy to the authenticated account so one business can never query another’s data.

chunks.title: Seasonal Demand
chunks.content: Seasonal Demand: The predictable rise and fall in call volume tied to weather and time of year — for example, HVAC cooling calls spiking in summer and heating calls spiking in winter.

chunks.title: Sentiment Analysis
chunks.content: Sentiment Analysis: The process of detecting a caller’s tone or emotional state — frustrated, urgent, satisfied — from their words and speech patterns, so calls can be prioritized or flagged for a human follow-up when needed.

chunks.title: Service Area
chunks.content: Service Area: The geographic region a business is willing and able to travel to for jobs. Confirming a caller is within the service area early in a call avoids wasted dispatch time.

chunks.title: SIP Trunking
chunks.content: SIP Trunking: A method of connecting a business phone system to the public phone network over the internet, using the Session Initiation Protocol. SIP trunking underlies most modern cloud-based call routing and forwarding setups.

chunks.title: SMS Text-Back
chunks.content: SMS Text-Back: An automatic text message sent to a caller within seconds of a missed or unanswered call, apologizing for missing them and including a link to book — so a lead isn’t lost just because nobody picked up in time.

chunks.title: SOC 2
chunks.content: SOC 2: An independent audit standard that evaluates how a company protects customer data across security, availability, and confidentiality. Businesses often ask vendors whether they are SOC 2 compliant before sharing customer information.

chunks.title: Speech-to-Text (STT)
chunks.content: Speech-to-Text (STT): The technology that converts a caller’s spoken words into written text in real time, so an AI system can interpret and respond to what was said. Accuracy in noisy environments — a caller standing outside near traffic, for example — is one of the harder problems in voice AI.

chunks.title: Single Sign-On (SSO)
chunks.content: Single Sign-On (SSO): A login system that lets a user access multiple connected tools with one set of credentials, reducing password fatigue and centralizing account security.

chunks.title: Technician Utilization
chunks.content: Technician Utilization: The percentage of a technician’s available working hours actually spent on billable jobs, as opposed to driving, waiting, or downtime.

chunks.title: Text-to-Speech (TTS)
chunks.content: Text-to-Speech (TTS): The technology that converts written text back into spoken audio, giving an AI receptionist its voice. Modern TTS engines produce natural pacing, tone, and inflection instead of the robotic cadence older systems were known for.

chunks.title: Time & Materials (T&M)
chunks.content: Time & Materials (T&M): A pricing model where the customer is billed based on the actual labor hours worked and materials used, rather than a single fixed quote.

chunks.title: Toll-Free Number
chunks.content: Toll-Free Number: A phone number, such as one starting with 800 or 888, that costs the caller nothing to dial. Some home service businesses use a toll-free number for marketing while keeping a local number for their main line. Using one to send SMS requires Toll-Free Verification with the carrier first, or messages get filtered.

chunks.title: Toll-Free Verification (TFV)
chunks.content: Toll-Free Verification (TFV): A one-time review carriers require before a toll-free number (800, 833, 844, 855, 866, 877, or 888) can send SMS reliably. You submit your business identity and how you plan to use the number; until it’s approved, texts from that number can be filtered or blocked outright. It is a separate process from 10DLC, which covers local numbers instead.

chunks.title: Truck Roll
chunks.content: Truck Roll: Sending a technician and vehicle out to a physical job site. Every truck roll has a real cost in fuel, labor, and time, which is why accurate information gathered before dispatch matters so much.

chunks.title: Turn-Taking
chunks.content: Turn-Taking: The back-and-forth rhythm of a conversation — knowing when to speak and when to listen. Good turn-taking is what separates a natural-sounding AI call from one that feels like talking to a phone tree.

chunks.title: Two-Way Sync
chunks.content: Two-Way Sync: A data connection where updates flow in both directions between two systems — a change made in one, like a rescheduled appointment, automatically reflects in the other.

chunks.title: Upsell
chunks.content: Upsell: Offering a customer an additional or higher-value service related to their original request — for example, suggesting a maintenance plan alongside a one-time repair.

chunks.title: Voice AI
chunks.content: Voice AI: The umbrella term for AI systems that operate through spoken conversation rather than text or a screen. Voice AI combines speech-to-text, language understanding, and text-to-speech into a single real-time experience.

chunks.title: Voicemail
chunks.content: Voicemail: A recorded message left when a call goes unanswered. Voicemail was built for an era when callers expected to wait for a callback — an expectation most callers no longer have, especially for urgent home service needs.

chunks.title: VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol)
chunks.content: VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol): Technology that carries phone calls over the internet instead of traditional copper phone lines. VoIP is what makes it possible for an AI receptionist to answer, route, and record calls without any special hardware at your office.

chunks.title: Warm Transfer
chunks.content: Warm Transfer: A call transfer where the receiving person is briefed on the caller’s situation before being connected, so the customer doesn’t have to repeat themselves from scratch.

chunks.title: Webhook
chunks.content: Webhook: An automated message sent from one system to another the moment a specific event happens — for example, notifying a CRM instantly when a new call is completed, rather than on a delay or a fixed schedule.

chunks.title: Work Order
chunks.content: Work Order: The internal record of a job — customer details, issue description, technician assigned, and status — used to track a request from the initial call through completion.

chunks.title: Zapier
chunks.content: Zapier: A no-code automation platform that connects thousands of apps together, letting non-technical teams build custom workflows — such as sending a text message whenever a new lead is captured.

chunks.title: Can I cancel anytime?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Billing & Plans. Q: Can I cancel anytime?
A: Yes, from Dashboard → Billing. There’s no long-term contract requirement for standard plans — check your plan details for the exact terms that apply to your account.

chunks.title: How is Vireek priced?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Billing & Plans. Q: How is Vireek priced?
A: Plans are based on call volume and features. Compare current plans on the Pricing page, or use the Revenue Calculator to estimate what missed calls are costing you today versus a Vireek plan.

chunks.title: What happens if I go over my plan’s call limit?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Billing & Plans. Q: What happens if I go over my plan’s call limit?
A: You’ll get a usage alert (in-app and via the Notification Center) as you approach your limit so you can upgrade before it affects call answering. We don’t cut off calls without warning you first.

chunks.title: Where do I manage billing and invoices?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Billing & Plans. Q: Where do I manage billing and invoices?
A: Dashboard → Billing shows your current plan, usage against your call allowance, and past invoices, and lets you update your payment method or change plans.

chunks.title: Can I customize what Sarah says?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Call Handling & Sarah. Q: Can I customize what Sarah says?
A: Yes, from Dashboard → Business Profile. You control the greeting, service list, hours, FAQ answers, qualifying questions, and who calls get escalated to. Changes take effect on the next call — no redeployment needed.

chunks.title: Can Sarah handle emergency calls?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Call Handling & Sarah. Q: Can Sarah handle emergency calls?
A: Yes. Sarah is trained to recognize urgent language, gather the key safety and location details, and immediately flag the call for fast follow-up. Sarah is not a replacement for 911 or licensed emergency dispatch, but she makes sure a real emergency never sits in a voicemail queue.

chunks.title: What does Sarah actually do on a call?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Call Handling & Sarah. Q: What does Sarah actually do on a call?
A: Sarah answers with your greeting, asks the qualifying questions relevant to your trade (service needed, address, urgency, availability), and captures the details your team needs — then books an appointment, logs a lead, or escalates, depending on what the caller needs.

chunks.title: What happens when Sarah can’t answer a caller’s question?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Call Handling & Sarah. Q: What happens when Sarah can’t answer a caller’s question?
A: Sarah will offer to take a message, schedule a callback, or transfer to your designated escalation contact based on the rules you set in Business Profile, rather than guessing or ending the call.

chunks.title: Can I see revenue and performance trends?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Dashboard & Reporting. Q: Can I see revenue and performance trends?
A: Yes. Dashboard → Analytics breaks down call volume, answer rate, lead conversion, and estimated revenue recovered over any date range. Dashboard → Insights adds AI-generated summaries of what changed and why.

chunks.title: Is my dashboard data live?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Dashboard & Reporting. Q: Is my dashboard data live?
A: Yes. Calls, Jobs, and the Overview stat cards update in real time. A small Live / Reconnecting indicator next to the page title shows the current connection status.

chunks.title: What’s the difference between Leads and Jobs?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Dashboard & Reporting. Q: What’s the difference between Leads and Jobs?
A: Leads (Dashboard → Leads) are captured inquiries that haven’t been converted yet. Jobs (Dashboard → Jobs) are confirmed, scheduled work with a status you can move through your pipeline (scheduled, in progress, completed, cancelled).

chunks.title: Where do I see my calls?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Dashboard & Reporting. Q: Where do I see my calls?
A: Dashboard → Calls shows every conversation Sarah has handled in real time, including a transcript, caller intent, and outcome. New calls appear at the top the moment they finish — no refresh needed.

chunks.title: Can I test Sarah before going live?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Getting Started. Q: Can I test Sarah before going live?
A: Yes. Use the Live Demo on the marketing site or place a call to your forwarded number after setup to hear exactly what your customers will hear, then adjust the script from your Business Profile.

chunks.title: Do I need to change my business phone number?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Getting Started. Q: Do I need to change my business phone number?
A: No. Keep the number your customers already know. Most businesses simply forward calls to Vireek (all calls, after-hours only, or overflow when your line is busy) so Sarah answers under the same number.

chunks.title: How do I create a Vireek account?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Getting Started. Q: How do I create a Vireek account?
A: Go to the Sign Up page and create your account with a work email and password. You will move straight into a short onboarding flow where you tell Sarah about your business — industry, service area, hours, and how you want calls handled.

chunks.title: How long does setup take?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Getting Started. Q: How long does setup take?
A: Most businesses are live within about 15 minutes: create an account, complete the Business Profile (services, hours, FAQs, escalation contact), forward your calls, and place a test call to confirm the greeting sounds right.

chunks.title: An integration shows as disconnected. What should I do?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Integrations. Q: An integration shows as disconnected. What should I do?
A: Reconnect it from Dashboard → Integrations — this usually resolves an expired authorization. If it reconnects and then drops again, contact support so we can check the connection logs on our side.

chunks.title: Does Sarah book directly onto my calendar?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Integrations. Q: Does Sarah book directly onto my calendar?
A: Yes — appointments booked during a call are written to Dashboard → Calendar and, where connected, synced to your integrated calendar so there’s one source of truth for scheduling.

chunks.title: Does Vireek integrate with my CRM?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Integrations. Q: Does Vireek integrate with my CRM?
A: Dashboard → Integrations lists the connections available for your plan. Vireek captures structured call and lead data specifically so it can flow into your existing tools instead of living in a separate silo.

chunks.title: Can I turn off certain notification types?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Notifications & Alerts. Q: Can I turn off certain notification types?
A: Yes. Dashboard → Settings lets you toggle email and SMS alerts independently for emergencies, new bookings, and usage warnings, without turning off in-app notifications.

chunks.title: How do I get notified about an emergency call?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Notifications & Alerts. Q: How do I get notified about an emergency call?
A: Emergency calls automatically create a notification (bell icon in the dashboard header) and, if enabled, an email or SMS alert. Configure exactly which events notify you at Dashboard → Settings → Notification Preferences.

chunks.title: Where can I see my full notification history?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Notifications & Alerts. Q: Where can I see my full notification history?
A: Dashboard → Notifications keeps a complete, searchable history and lets you mark items as read individually or all at once.

chunks.title: How is my customer call data protected?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Security & Privacy. Q: How is my customer call data protected?
A: Data is protected with encryption in transit and at rest, strict database-level access rules (Row Level Security) scoped to your account, and role-based permissions so team members only ever see what they’re allowed to. See the full Security page for details.

chunks.title: What are trusted devices?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Security & Privacy. Q: What are trusted devices?
A: When you verify a new device during login, you can mark it as trusted so future sign-ins from that device skip extra verification. Manage or revoke trusted devices anytime from Dashboard → Settings → Security.

chunks.title: What is the Audit Log?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Security & Privacy. Q: What is the Audit Log?
A: Dashboard → Settings → Security records sensitive account changes — team permission changes, job deletions, billing plan changes, business profile edits, and integration connect/disconnect events — as an append-only log for accountability.

chunks.title: Where do I read the full privacy policy?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Security & Privacy. Q: Where do I read the full privacy policy?
A: The complete Privacy Policy and Terms of Service are always available in the site footer and explain exactly what data is collected, why, and how long it’s kept.

chunks.title: A team member says they aren’t seeing new calls update live. What’s going on?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Team & Permissions. Q: A team member says they aren’t seeing new calls update live. What’s going on?
A: Realtime updates are scoped to your account, not to any single login, so this should work automatically. If it doesn’t, ask them to refresh the page once — if the issue persists, contact support with their account email.

chunks.title: Can I limit what a team member sees?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Team & Permissions. Q: Can I limit what a team member sees?
A: Yes. Roles control access — for example, a technician can be limited to only the jobs assigned to them, while an office manager can see every call, lead, and job across the account.

chunks.title: How do I invite a team member?
chunks.content:
Help Center — Team & Permissions. Q: How do I invite a team member?
A: Go to Dashboard → Team and send an invite by email. The invite includes a secure sign-up link, and you can resend it if it expires before they accept.

chunks.title: A caller says Sarah didn’t understand them.
chunks.content:
Help Center — Troubleshooting. Q: A caller says Sarah didn’t understand them.
A: Background noise and heavy accents can occasionally affect recognition. Check the call transcript in Dashboard → Calls — if it’s a recurring pattern rather than a one-off, send us the call ID so we can review it.

chunks.title: Calls aren’t reaching Sarah.
chunks.content:
Help Center — Troubleshooting. Q: Calls aren’t reaching Sarah.
A: Double-check the call-forwarding number configured with your phone carrier matches the number shown in Dashboard → Business Profile exactly, including country code. Most issues come from a forwarding rule pointing at the wrong number or being scoped to “busy only” instead of “no answer.”

chunks.title: I don’t see a booked appointment on my calendar.
chunks.content:
Help Center — Troubleshooting. Q: I don’t see a booked appointment on my calendar.
A: Confirm the integration is still connected at Dashboard → Integrations, then check Dashboard → Calendar directly, since a booking always lands there first regardless of external sync status.

chunks.title: I’m not receiving email or SMS alerts.
chunks.content:
Help Center — Troubleshooting. Q: I’m not receiving email or SMS alerts.
A: Check Dashboard → Settings → Notification Preferences to confirm the relevant toggle is on, and check your spam folder for the sending address. If alerts still don’t arrive, contact support.

chunks.title: Appliance Repair: Can it capture the appliance brand and model over the phone?
chunks.content:
Q: Can it capture the appliance brand and model over the phone?
A: Yes. Vireek asks the same qualifying questions a trained dispatcher would, so your technician arrives with the right information.

chunks.title: Appliance Repair: Can it separate warranty calls from paid service calls?
chunks.content:
Q: Can it separate warranty calls from paid service calls?
A: Yes. Vireek captures warranty status on the call and routes the booking accordingly.

chunks.title: Vireek for Appliance Repair
chunks.content: A dead fridge or washer is urgent to the customer. Sarah treats it that way. Common call reasons: Refrigerator repair, washer/dryer, dishwasher, oven/range, warranty service. Pain points: A broken refrigerator is a same-day emergency to the customer, even if it is routine to your team. Diagnosing the likely issue and brand/model over the phone takes time your office staff does not have. Warranty and non-warranty calls need different handling but often get mixed together. How Vireek handles it: Answers instantly and captures appliance type, brand, symptom, and warranty status. Books diagnostic and repair visits directly onto your calendar based on real availability. Flags high-urgency situations like a fridge full of spoiling food for faster scheduling.

chunks.title: Cleaning Services: Can existing clients reschedule without waiting for a callback?

Legal Service Level Agreement Last updated: September 12, 2026 Introduction & Scope This Service Level Agreement ("SLA") describes the uptime commitment Vireek makes to customers on paid subscription plans for the core Vireek platform (call answering, dashboard access, and the customer-facing API). It does not apply to customers on a free plan or during a free trial. Uptime Commitment Vireek targets a 99. 9% monthly uptime for the core platform on all paid plans. Enterprise customers may negotiate a custom uptime commitment and credit schedule as part of a signed order form. Monthly uptime percentage is calculated as: (total minutes in the calendar month minutes of Downtime) total minutes in the calendar month 100. What Counts as Downtime "Downtime" means the core platform is unavailable or fails to answer inbound calls for reasons within Vireek's reasonable control, as confirmed by our monitoring systems or a verified customer report. Brief periods of elevated latency that do not prevent calls from being answered do not count as Downtime. Exclusions The following are excluded from Downtime calculations: • Scheduled maintenance announced at least 24 hours in advance • Outages caused by the customer's own equipment, network, or misconfiguration • Outages of third-party telephony carriers, SMS gateways, or integration partners outside Vireek's infrastructure • Force majeure events (natural disasters, war, widespread internet or power outages, government action) • Suspension of an account for a Terms of Service violation or non-payment Service Credits If actual monthly uptime falls below the commitment in Section 2, eligible customers receive a credit toward a future invoice: • Below 99. 9% but at or above 99. 0% — 10% of that month's subscription fee • Below 99. 0% but at or above 95. 0% — 25% of that month's subscription fee • Below 95. 0% — 50% of that month's subscription fee

chunks.title: Answer every call after hours, without being on call
chunks.content: Nights, weekends and holidays are covered. Sarah handles the call your way and has everything ready for you in the morning. Situation: It’s 11 pm on a Saturday. A customer wants a quote for a repair they’ve been putting off. Nobody is in the office, and by Monday they’ve booked someone else. Without Vireek: After-hours calls go to voicemail, and most callers don’t leave a message. Owners carry the phone everywhere just in case. Monday starts with a pile of callbacks and no idea which ones matter. With Vireek: Sarah answers every after-hours call, day or night. Calls are routed by the rules you set for your hours. Messages to callers reflect whether you’re open or closed. How it works: 1. Set your hours — Tell Vireek when you’re open and how you want closed hours handled. 2. Sarah answers when you’re closed — Callers get a real conversation instead of a voicemail beep. 3. Calls are routed by urgency — Routine requests are booked or queued; true emergencies can escalate to your on-call team. 4. A morning-ready handoff — Every overnight call is logged with a summary, so you start the day knowing who to call first. Outcomes: Open around the clock: Your business sounds available even when your office isn’t. Rest without risk: Routine calls wait for morning; emergencies can still reach your on-call team. A calmer Monday: Callbacks are organized with context instead of a pile of voicemails. Plan note: 24/7 AI call answering is on every plan. Custom after-hours routing is included on Professional and above.

chunks.title: Get real emergencies to a real person, fast
chunks.content: Vireek spots urgent calls the moment they come in and transfers them live to your on-call team, instead of letting them sit in a queue. Situation: A pipe bursts at 9 pm. The homeowner calls three companies, and the first one that connects them with a real person gets the job. Without Vireek: Urgent calls and routine calls wait in the same voicemail box. Your on-call tech finds out about the emergency long after the customer called someone else. Nobody can tell a burst pipe from a dripping faucet until they call back. With Vireek: Sarah triages every call against the emergency triggers you define. Matching calls are transferred live to your on-call number or ring group. If nobody picks up, Sarah stays with the caller and flags the lead as urgent. How it works: 1. Sarah detects the emergency — Language that matches your trigger conditions, like no heat or a burst pipe, marks the call as urgent. 2. The call is transferred live — A warm transfer connects the caller to your on-call number or ring group, with context. 3. Barge-in when it helps — Optionally join a call in progress when a second set of ears is useful. 4. A safe fallback — If no one answers, Sarah keeps the caller, captures the details and flags the job as urgent. Outcomes: Speed where it counts: The calls that can’t wait reach a person first. Rules you control: You decide what counts as an emergency and who gets the call. Nothing falls through: Even unanswered transfers end with a captured, flagged lead. Plan note: Emergency detection and live dispatch are included on Professional and above.

chunks.title: Close more estimates without chasing them
chunks.content: Quotes that go quiet don’t have to die. Vireek keeps customers answered, informed and nudged toward a decision while you work. Situation: You sent an estimate on Tuesday. By Thursday the customer is “still thinking about it,” and you’re too busy bidding the next job to chase it. Without Vireek: Follow-up depends on you remembering between jobs. Customers with a quick question reach voicemail and cool off. You can’t tell which estimates are still alive. With Vireek: Customers who call about an estimate reach Sarah, not voicemail. Follow-up goes out automatically instead of waiting on you. Accepted estimates are easy to move onto the schedule. How it works: 1. The estimate goes out — Customers receive a quote they can review and accept online. 2. Questions get answered — When a customer calls with a question, Sarah answers and logs the conversation to the lead record. 3. Follow-up happens automatically — A timely nudge keeps the estimate from going cold while you’re on another job. 4. Accepted work gets scheduled — Once the customer says yes, booking the job takes one step, not a game of phone tag. Outcomes: More estimates answered: Customers get a response while they’re still deciding. Less manual chasing: Follow-up stops depending on your memory between jobs. A clear pipeline: See which estimates are open, discussed or accepted.

chunks.title: Turn missed calls into booked jobs
chunks.content: Every call you can’t pick up is answered, qualified and followed up — before the caller dials the next company on the list. Situation: It’s mid-afternoon and your whole crew is on a job. A homeowner with a leaking water heater calls, reaches voicemail and moves on to the next search result. You find out hours later — if at all. Without Vireek: Callers hang up on voicemail and call a competitor. You spend your evening returning calls to people who already booked elsewhere. There is no record of who called, what they needed or how urgent it was. With Vireek: Sarah answers instantly and finds out what the caller needs. If the call drops, the caller gets a text with your booking link. Every call becomes a structured lead in your dashboard. How it works: 1. A call comes in while you’re busy — Sarah, your AI receptionist, answers the calls you can’t take. 2. The lead is qualified — Name, address, service needed and urgency are captured, with a service-area check. 3. A text goes out automatically — If the caller hangs up early, a branded text with your booking link is sent within seconds. 4. You get the full picture — A call summary and the lead record land in your dashboard, ready for your CRM. Outcomes: Fewer lost leads: Callers reach someone every time, so fewer of them turn into a competitor’s customer. Less phone tag: You call back with context instead of starting from “who is this and what do they need?” A record of every call: See who called, why and what happened next, without digging through voicemail.
